parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national layer carries documented, traveller-facing exposures. Entry screening refuses cases on any document-sex discrepancy and can impose a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding. Passport markers are restricted, and some trans travellers were stranded abroad. Immigration custody shows documented forced labour and sexual abuse, and national corrections adopted conversion-style policies. Federal counterterrorism framing names 'radically pro-transgender' groups. The division's operative protections are real and visitor-facing: public-accommodations non-discrimination, gender-identity hate-crime enhancement, shield laws, and a minors' conversion-therapy ban. It documents no bathroom criminalisation. Under the override, these do not cancel federal entry and custody exposure. Enforcement data for the protections is absent, so they are credited only as documented in force.

entry_documents.exposure: Cable instructs refusal on any document or record discrepancy or reasonable doubt about sex. Adjudicators may consider a permanent fraud ineligibility finding. Passports with markers not matching birth sex are blocked or confiscated, leaving some travellers stranded. Airport screening can trigger outing via pat-downs.
entry_documents.protection: Visitors use home-country passports. Some individual travellers are not affected. The fraud ground requires all four elements and is not automatic. Litigation is ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal entry screening governs the traveller regardless of the division's non-discrimination law. A mismatch can move from refusal to fraud allegation to detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Federal corrections adopted conversion-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court challenges pending. No documented protective custody placement for trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal custody applies to any visitor detained at entry, whatever the division's protections. The division's laws do not reach federal detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National government-funded single-sex facilities bar gender-identity-congruent access. Four states criminalise certain trans restroom use. In one, a trespass charge followed a 2025 arrest, with handcuffing and 24 hours in men's custody. Facility bans in 9 states plus one unit cover all government buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division bathroom status is not documented as restricted. Single-user public bathrooms in the division are gender-neutral since 2018.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitors crossing into restricted states meet the criminal trespass exposure. The division's own facilities rules are not documented as restrictive.

care_services.exposure: Federal subpoenas of over 20 hospitals for under-19 records. Proposed federal rule would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. Specialised youth crisis services were shut down.
care_services.protection: Division shield laws (2023, 2024) are enforceable against out-of-state action. Division insurers have been required to cover trans care since 2013.
care_services.interaction: A visitor seeking care in the division is shielded from out-of-state action. Federal subpoenas and rules can still reach records and funding.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups alongside anarchists. A December 2025 reward system references 'radical gender ideology'. Officials frame trans advocacy in security terms.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target those who merely disagree. No documented operational targeting of visitors is recorded.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Security framing at federal level sits above the division's protective posture and may amplify scrutiny of advocates.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal executive order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition, including preferred names. Under-18 care reimbursement bar proposed. Gender-affirming care for children is banned in 27 states. Minors' documents may mismatch at entry.
minors_guardians.protection: Division anti-bullying law covers gender identity and sexual orientation in all schools. Division conversion-therapy ban treats the practice on minors as unprofessional conduct. Division education policy protects trans students.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor's care or school needs may be disrupted by federal rules. A guardian faces entry scrutiny of a minor's documents. Division protections cover minors while they are in the division.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity. Only 23 states cover gender identity in bias statutes; 37 lacked them as of 2019. Bias against sexual orientation accounts for about one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias incidents. No trans-specific violence rate is given.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division gender-identity hate-crime enhancement, repealed gay and trans panic defence (2021), and public-accommodations non-discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Division protections operate for visitors in the division. The arrest for bathroom trespass in a restricted state shows police exposure in the national layer.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal remedies are under challenge and several orders are enjoined. Division enforcement data for the hate-crime provision and public-accommodations complaints is not sourced. Travel advisories from allied governments.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division protections are in force. Legal-aid FAQ and shield laws offer recourse for care. Civil-liberties litigation against the passport restrictions is running.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists for some federal actions but has not been shown to reverse entry or custody harms. Uncertainty over which measures are in effect at travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower anchor: birth-sex housing, criminal cross-dressing statute, and documented prison assaults with no protective transfers. Our case lacks a local criminal cross-dressing offence and has division shield and anti-discrimination protections. It sits higher, but the documented federal immigration custody abuse keeps it near this tier.

Universal entry exclusion of trans visitors with routine enforcement and no effective appeal. Our case is conditional on document discrepancy, with a discretionary refusal and a possible but non-automatic lifetime fraud finding. Division protections add recourse. It sits slightly higher.

Secondary screening, humiliating searches and administrative refusal at ports, with slow remedies. Our case has a similar border layer but adds documented custody abuse and federal facility bans. Division protections offset some of this, so it sits roughly similar to slightly lower.

Upper-middle anchor with operating protections, police accountability and effective assault response. Our case has documented division protections but federal entry and custody exposures that the division cannot cancel. It would need federal entry and custody harms removed to reach this tier.

parsed.synthesis: Federal entry screening, passport restrictions and federal custody with documented sexual abuse and conversion-style policies are the operative exposures. They reach any visitor with a document discrepancy and any detained visitor. Division protections (public accommodations, hate-crime enhancement, shield laws, minors' conversion-therapy ban) operate and mitigate in the division. They do not cancel federal exposures, and the bathroom trespass arrest shows the national layer reaching travellers. Net: elevated risk, toward the upper end of the band because of division protections, but below the 0.55 tier.
